blocks.text: 1. Diffusion Models

blocks.alt: A clean image has noise added gradually until it becomes pure noise

blocks.text: GANs' own closing recap, already covered in GANs, pointed forward here. Diffusion Models, a newer generative approach built on a fundamentally different training idea, take yet another distinct path to generation.
They genuinely learn to reverse a gradual noising process step by step, an idea explored in full throughout this topic.

3. The Forward Diffusion Process

blocks.alt: A clean image passes through steps into a noisy image

blocks.text: This connects back to real training data, already covered generally across this course. The forward process genuinely adds a small amount of random noise to an image over many separate steps.
After genuinely enough steps, the original image genuinely becomes indistinguishable from pure random noise, a genuinely deliberate, controlled corruption explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. The Reverse Process

blocks.alt: Pure noise passes through denoise steps back into a clean image

blocks.text: This connects back to the forward diffusion process, already covered in this topic. The reverse process genuinely trains a network to undo that noising, one small step at a time.
Starting from genuinely pure random noise, it genuinely walks backward toward a realistic image, the exact mechanism that makes generation possible, explored throughout the rest of this topic.
5. Predicting The Noise

blocks.alt: A noisy image goes through a model to predict the noise

blocks.text: This connects back to the reverse process, already covered in this topic. At every single step, the network's own actual task is genuinely simple: predict the noise that was added.
Genuinely subtracting that predicted noise moves the image one small step closer to realistic, a genuinely simple, repeated prediction task explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This simple, repeated prediction task, already covered in this topic, directly explains why diffusion models can be trained with a genuinely straightforward loss, comparing predicted noise against actually added noise.

blocks.text: 6. Many Small Steps Versus One Big Leap

blocks.alt: One big leap is compared against many small steps

blocks.text: This connects back to predicting the noise, already covered in this topic. Diffusion genuinely breaks generation into many small, individually easy steps.

This happens rather than a GAN's own generator, already covered in GANs, attempting one single big leap from noise to image, a genuinely fundamental structural difference explored throughout the rest of this topic.
7. Why Diffusion Trains More Stably

blocks.alt: GAN adversarial training is unstable while diffusion trains stably

blocks.text: This connects back to many small steps versus one big leap, already covered in this topic. Each genuinely small denoising step is a genuinely much easier learning target.
This genuinely avoids the adversarial instability already covered as mode collapse in GANs, a genuinely real practical advantage explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 8. Sampling Speed Tradeoff

blocks.alt: Diffusion needs many steps while GAN needs one pass

blocks.text: This connects back to many small steps, already covered in this topic. Genuinely generating one sample requires running through genuinely many reverse steps in sequence.

This genuinely makes diffusion sampling considerably slower than a GAN's own single forward pass, already covered in GANs, a genuinely real cost weighed against the training stability already covered earlier in this topic.
9. Recognizing When Diffusion Models Are Genuinely The Right Choice

This connects back to genuinely needing the highest possible generation quality and stable training, already covered in this topic. Diffusion Models, already covered in this topic, directly deliver exactly that quality.
This connects back to GANs, already covered, favoring genuinely faster generation speed instead. GANs, already covered, remain genuinely preferable when generation speed matters more.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a simplified forward and reverse diffusion process, already covered in this topic, on a single numeric value.

code.content:
import random
random.seed(0)

def forward_step(x, noise_scale=0.3):
    # already covered as the forward diffusion process in this topic
    noise = random.gauss(0, 1)
    return x + noise_scale * noise, noise

def reverse_step(x_noisy, predicted_noise, noise_scale=0.3):
    # already covered as the reverse process predicting and subtracting noise in this topic
    return x_noisy - noise_scale * predicted_noise

original = 1.0  # already covered as a real value from training data in this topic
x = original
noises = []

print("Forward process (already covered in this topic), adding noise step by step:")
for step in range(4):
    x, noise = forward_step(x)
    noises.append(noise)
    print(f"  step {step+1}: x={x:.3f}")

print("\nReverse process (already covered in this topic), removing noise step by step:")
for step, noise in enumerate(reversed(noises)):
    # already covered as predicting the noise in this topic
    x = reverse_step(x, noise)
    print(f"  step {step+1}: x={x:.3f}")

print(f"\nRecovered value: {x:.3f}, original was: {original}")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Diffusion models learn to reverse a gradual noising process step by step.
The forward process adds small amounts of noise until an image becomes pure random noise.
The reverse process trains a network to undo that noising, starting from pure noise.
At each step, the network's task is simple: predict the noise that was added, then subtract it.
Diffusion breaks generation into many small steps, unlike a GAN's single big leap.
Small, easy learning targets make diffusion training more stable than adversarial GAN training.
Generating one sample requires many sequential reverse steps, making sampling slower than a GAN.
Diffusion models suit tasks needing top generation quality and stable training over raw speed.
